purpose: Teach: 東方/長寿/祈願/武術/癒す/ユートピア/迷信/懐中

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが東方の音楽、つまり東方民謡を愛された
lines.en: Dear, when I was young, my father loved the music of the East — the old eastern folk songs.
lines.style: Slow low reminiscence, long pauses between phrases; gaze somewhere far away, words chosen carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、長寿研究の文献を蔵書されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm, and you, Grandpa — you collected all those books on longevity research back then, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Soft papery warmth, slow affectionate lilt; rising gently on the tag question, teasing kindly.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが神社で祈願された
lines.en: Dear, in those days my father would go and offer prayers at the shrine.
lines.style: Quiet contemplative delivery, breath audible before speaking; the memory arriving before the words do.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、武術の稽古に通われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you went off to your martial arts practice in those days, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Fond slow recollection with a small knowing smile; gentle emphasis on 'you', savoring the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「音楽が心を癒す」と仰った
lines.en: Dear, my father used to say that music heals the heart.
lines.style: Hushed reverence on the quoted words, slowing almost to a stop; voice softened by the years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、ユートピア論を熱く語られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you used to hold forth so passionately about utopias, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm amused wobble, nearly a laugh on 'passionately'; affectionate rising tag, eyes crinkling.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが村の迷信を研究された
lines.en: Dear, my father made a study of the village superstitions, you know.
lines.style: Measured, gently philosophical delivery; a scholar's respect in the pacing, trailing thoughtfully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、懐中時計を肌身離さず持ってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And that pocket watch — you never once let it out of your sight, did you, dear?
lines.style: Slow loving close, voice dipping near a whisper; the tag question held soft and long.
